newsitem.title: ITALY: Venice flooded, rivers break banks in stormy Italy.
newsitem.headline: Venice flooded, rivers break banks in stormy Italy.

text.p: Venice was under more than a metre (three feet) of flood water on Monday and rivers swelled to overflowing in many parts of central and northern Italy as heavy rainstorms lashed the country.
Civil protection officials raised flood alarms in several areas of Tuscany, Umbria and Liguria, where rivers and streams broke their banks. No serious injuries were reported.
Weather officials said the next 24 hours would be critical and the rains were expected to continue in many areas.
The River Tiber flooded near Orte, north of Rome, and in the central region of Umbria the River Nera overflowed and cut off a railway line near the city of Narni.
Officials evacuated gypsies from a low-lying area in northern Rome in case the Tiber overflowed there.
In Venice, alarm sirens sounded twice in the lagoon city overnight to warn residents to expect floods.
Many Venetians had to wade to work on Monday. One resident was shown on Italian television giving a woman a piggy-back through St Mark's Square.
Foreign tourists tip-toed with their luggage along sodden gangplanks laid out above the water.
The city's flood monitoring centre said water levels hit 1.34 metres at 7.30 a.m. (0630 GMT), the 16th highest this century, before the tide turned and waters started to recede.
It said further flooding was expected on Tuesday, with levels reaching 1.2 metres.
Monday's floods covered about 80 percent of the city, which is built on wooden piles buried deep in the Venice lagoon.
Officials said levels had exceeded forecasts after unexpected high winds, gusting up to 90 kph (55 mph), drove in the high tide.
